title: How can one known product help us find the next?
description: Fifty three times eighteen is known to be nine hundred and fifty four. Sixty three is written as fifty three plus ten, the bracket is opened, and ten more lots of eighteen are added. Keeko doubts that only ten is added.
teaching_notes: One idea: when one number in a product grows by ten, the product grows by ten whole lots of the other number. Watch for students who add only ten to the known product.

video_script.why: A learner sees how a known product and a bracket give a new product without multiplying again.
video_script.substitution: Replace fifty three and ten with any known number and any change, and the same bracket works.
video_script.anchor: fifty three lots of eighteen drawn as a block, with ten more lots of eighteen added beside it
video_script.wrong_answer: we add only ten to nine hundred and fifty four
video_script.wrong_move: adds 10 to 954, but the 10 more lots are each worth 18
video_script.payoff_line: Sixty three times eighteen is one thousand one hundred and thirty four.

final_answer.spoken: sixty three times eighteen is one thousand one hundred and thirty four

video_script.design: A block of fifty three rows of eighteen with ten more rows of eighteen added. The bracket opens into the known product plus the new lots.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the known fact 53 × 18 = 954 and the unknown 63 × 18 side by side

marks.h4: the words without multiplying afresh are written

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about a known product.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>We know that fifty three times eighteen is nine hundred and fifty four.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>We want sixty three times eighteen.
<bookmark mark='h4'/>How can we find it without multiplying afresh?

beats.on_screen: both products stay on the board and the question mark keeps glowing

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a block of 53 rows of 18, then 63 rows of 18 with ten extra rows shaded

marks.g1: the block of fifty three rows of eighteen is drawn
marks.g2: the block grows to sixty three rows
marks.g3: the ten extra rows are shaded

beats.colours: the ten extra rows in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Fifty three times eighteen means fifty three lots of eighteen.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Sixty three times eighteen means sixty three lots of eighteen.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Sixty three lots has ten lots more than fifty three lots.
<bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, fifty three times eighteen is nine hundred and fifty four.

marks.fd1: 63 × 18 is written with a question mark

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to find sixty three times eighteen without multiplying again.

marks.s12: the sum goes inside a bracket with 18 outside

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, write sixty three as fifty three plus ten, because sixty three is ten more.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>Sixty three times eighteen is open bracket fifty three plus ten close bracket times eighteen.

marks.s21: the 18 is copied after 53 and after 10

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, remove the bracket, because the eighteen multiplies each term inside it.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>This gives fifty three times eighteen plus ten times eighteen.
<bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, put in the known value, nine hundred and fifty four.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>Ten times eighteen is one hundred and eighty.
We add nine hundred and fifty four and one hundred and eighty.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>Sixty three times eighteen is one thousand one hundred and thirty four.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 954 + 10; it is struck out and the ten shaded rows of 18 are shown

marks.k3: the ten shaded rows each light up with eighteen

narration: <bookmark mark='k2'/>Keeko thinks we add only ten to nine hundred and fifty four.
<bookmark mark='k3'/>But sixty three is ten more than fifty three, and the ten is multiplied by eighteen.
<bookmark mark='k4'/>Each extra one adds one whole eighteen.
